page: OVHcloud b2-120 is a general-purpose server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs using the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Haswell processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 120.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 400 GB SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the bottom 10% and Geekbench single-core scores in the bottom 25%. However, the 32 dedicated physical cores compensate in parallelized tasks, elevating multi-core metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, to average levels. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks also performs within the middle 50% range.

The instance exhibits weak performance in text processing and single-threaded operations, making it less suitable for sequential execution paths. For LLM workloads, while prompt processing for small and medium models achieves average speeds, text generation is weak to poor, and large model execution is constrained. Qualitatively, the b2-120 offers a balanced resource density of compute and memory for parallelized workloads. It is suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, database operations, and software compilation where parallel execution can offset the lower single-core clock speed.
